extracted.intended_audience: readers and producers of the periodical (early-18th-century literate public; patrons/subscribers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and stated principles for creating and publishing a weekly/tri-weekly periodical (the Tatler): its purpose, tone, format, audience, topical organization, distribution, and use of contributions. Geared to producing short essays, news-letters, and entertainments for a broad public.

rubrics_metrics.name: General purpose of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The general purpose of this paper, is to expose the false arts of life, to pull off the disguises of cunning, vanity, and affectation, and recommend a general simplicity in our dress, our discourse, and our behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim pieces at exposing social impostures and promoting simplicity; authors should use the paper to correct manners and vices rather than mere partisan attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and method
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man has no design but to speak plain truth, he may say a great deal in a very narrow compass... treat of [obvious and common subjects] in a new and unbeaten method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak plain truth; treat ordinary/common subjects freshly and originally; combine honesty with wit — wit without useful end is frivolous. Avoid being carried away by fashion or prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form / literary shape
rubrics_metrics.description: To make this generally read, it seemed the most proper method to form it by way of a letter of intelligence, consisting of such parts as might gratify the curiosity of persons of all conditions, and of each sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conceit of an intelligence-letter as organizing device; include variety in parts to appeal across social classes and sexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall ... publish such my advices and reflections every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday in the week for the convenience of the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and adhere to a regular tri-weekly schedule timed to postal runs to maximise circulation and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical organization (by coffee-house/article headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: All accounts of gallantry, pleasure, and entertainment, shall be under the article of White's Chocolate-house; poetry, under that of Will's Coffee-house; learning, under the title of Grecian; foreign and domestic news, you will have from St. James's Coffee-house; and what else I shall on any other subject offer, shall be dated from my own apartment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content by recognizable social loci (coffee-houses) so readers can expect where to find particular kinds of material; date items by place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting and instructional aim
rubrics_metrics.description: This my paper ... should be principally intended for the use of politic persons, who are so public spirited as to neglect their own affairs to look into transactions of State ... wherein I shall from time to time report and consider all matters of what kind soever that shall occur to me, and publish such my advices and reflections...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address both politically-minded readers and the general public; include reporting and reflections intended to instruct 'politic' readers what to think while also entertaining other classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content selection — avoid dull official copy
rubrics_metrics.description: we shall not, upon a dearth of news, present you with musty foreign edicts, or dull proclamations, but shall divide our relation of the passages which occur in action or discourse throughout this town...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reprinting dry official proclamations; prefer lively accounts of occurrences in action or discourse (social anecdotes, entertainments, conversations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and distribution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: I therefore earnestly desire all persons, without distinction, to take it in for the present gratis, and hereafter at the price of one penny, forbidding all hawkers to take more for it at their peril.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launch gratis to build readership, then charge a low fixed price (one penny) thereafter; enforce price ceilings on hawkers to prevent overcharging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and use of contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: There are through the course of the work very many incidents which were written by unknown correspondents... I have only one gentleman, who will be nameless, to thank for any frequent assistance to me... This same hand writ the distinguishing characters... which I cannot but look upon as the greatest embellishments of this work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and print contributions from correspondents (often anonymous); recognize and acknowledge notable assistance where appropriate; use outside pieces to embellish the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial impartiality and praise of merit
rubrics_metrics.description: I think it is apparent, I have with the utmost frankness allowed merit wherever I found it, though joined in interests different from those for which I have declared myself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow and praise merit regardless of political or party alignment; defend impartiality and avoid being accused of partisan motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fantastical devices (predictions/divination) sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: I can, by casting a figure, tell you all that will happen before it comes to pass. But this last faculty I shall use very sparingly, and not speak of anything until it is passed, for fear of divulging matters which may offend our superiors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employing devices like predictions or satirical 'divination', use them sparingly and only after events to avoid real-world offense or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix of instruction and entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: The general purpose ... to observe upon the manners of the pleasureable, as well as the busy part of mankind. To make this generally read... consisting of such parts as might gratify the curiosity of persons of all conditions, and of each sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance moral instruction (observing manners) with entertainment and curiosity-gratifying material to broaden appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on local correspondence and observers
rubrics_metrics.description: I had settled a correspondence in all parts of the known and knowing world... the addition of the ordinary occurrences of common journals of news brought in a multitude of other readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a network of correspondents and local observers to supply varied and timely material rather than relying solely on official reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive editorial posture toward criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: I really have acted in these cases with honesty, and am concerned it should be thought otherwise... all that one should value himself upon in this kind is, that he had some honourable intention in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When criticized, defend the ethical intentions of the publication; assert honesty of purpose and avoid letting raillery be seen as partisan attack.
